sourcedFrom: EOTECH DCBL SOUND SUPPRESSOR manual — SP2501 REV A, NOVEMBER 2025 (2025)
cleanIntro: The DCBL 762 is one of the three models in EOTech's titanium DCBL suppressor line. One part comes off its body: the Hub, the threaded mount at the rear that takes EOTech's KFM flash hider. EOTech prints one cleaning for the whole can, at least every 2,000 rounds: Hub off, threads cleaned, body cleaned with a titanium-safe solvent, blown out and dry, Hub back on. Nothing past the Hub is opened. Everything about unloading your rifle comes from that rifle's own manual.

steps.title: Rifle unloaded, magazine out, safety on, chamber checked
steps.action: Before the can comes off, unload the rifle, take the magazine out and put the safety on. Then look into the chamber and see that it is clear.
steps.prose: Both hands are about to be at the muzzle. EOTech's book covers the suppressor, not the rifle, so how your rifle is unloaded comes from its own manual.
steps.quote: Before removing your suppressor, ensure the firearm is unloaded, the magazine is removed, and the safety is on. Visually check that the chamber is clear.
steps.cite: EOTECH DCBL SOUND SUPPRESSOR manual — SP2501 REV A, NOVEMBER 2025 — GET STARTED — Removal, p.7

steps.title: ⛔ Let it cool, and glove up
steps.action: Wait until the suppressor is cool before you touch it, and keep it off skin and clothing until then. Put protective gloves on before you handle it: they keep the lead fouling off your hands.
steps.prose: A can that has just been shot looks exactly like a cold one. Wash your hands when you are finished.
steps.aside: Wear protective gloves to reduce the exposure of lead.
steps.quote: Ensure your suppressor is cool before touching.
steps.cite: EOTECH DCBL SOUND SUPPRESSOR manual — SP2501 REV A, NOVEMBER 2025 — GET STARTED — Removal, p.7
steps.warn: The suppressor system can reach extremely hot temperatures. Use caution before handling after use. Avoid contact with skin or clothing when hot.

steps.title: What it has been fed, and on how much barrel
steps.action: Check that the ammunition matches the suppressor's caliber. EOTech's table lists the DCBL-762 with a 0.39 in. bore and a minimum barrel length of 10.3 in., and marks it not rated for full auto.
steps.prose: The same book covers the 556 and the 9PCC, and their figures are not this can's. Go by the marking on the can in your hand.
steps.quote: ALWAYS check that your ammunition caliber matches the caliber of your suppressor.
steps.cite: EOTECH DCBL SOUND SUPPRESSOR manual — SP2501 REV A, NOVEMBER 2025 — THE BASICS — Safety Warnings, p.6; Specifications, p.5

steps.title: Off the rifle: clockwise from a KFM, counter-clockwise from bare threads
steps.action: Grip the suppressor firmly and turn it. EOTech's removal page gives two directions: off the KFM muzzle device, turn clockwise, because that adapter uses reverse threads; otherwise turn counter-clockwise. Lift it off the threads and put the muzzle device or thread protector back on the barrel.
steps.prose: It went on hand tight, or about 20 ft-lb, so it should not need a fight. EOTech's installation page also prints clockwise for threading the Hub onto the muzzle device, which does not agree with a reverse thread. If yours gets tighter the way you are turning it, stop, and ask EOTech before you put force on it.
steps.aside: Grip the suppressor firmly and turn counter-clockwise.
steps.quote: If using the KFM muzzle device, turn clockwise (the adapter uses reverse threads).
steps.cite: EOTECH DCBL SOUND SUPPRESSOR manual — SP2501 REV A, NOVEMBER 2025 — GET STARTED — Removal, p.7

steps.title: Hub off the body with an armorer's tool
steps.action: Fit the armorer's tool to the Hub. Hold the suppressor body and crank the tool counter-clockwise until the Hub breaks loose, then keep turning until it comes away from the body.
steps.prose: The Hub went in at about 35 ft-lb, so expect one firm break and then easy turning. EOTech names no other way to start it.
steps.quote: Align the tool onto the hub, and while holding the suppressor body, crank the tool counter-clockwise to break it from the suppressor body. Continue to turn until it separates from the body.
steps.cite: EOTECH DCBL SOUND SUPPRESSOR manual — SP2501 REV A, NOVEMBER 2025 — MAINTENANCE — Disassembly, p.8

steps.title: ⛔ That is as far as it goes
steps.action: The Hub is the only part EOTech takes off the body. Nothing past it comes apart: EOTech describes the construction as monolithic and forbids going further than its manual shows.
steps.prose: A can that rattles, is damaged or will not come apart at the Hub goes to EOTech, not to a bigger tool. EOTech wants a Return Authorization Number and the ATF form before it is shipped.
steps.aside: Do not ship the suppressor without a Return Authorization Number and ATF FORM.
steps.quote: NEVER disassemble the suppressor beyond what is highlighted in this manual.
steps.cite: EOTECH DCBL SOUND SUPPRESSOR manual — SP2501 REV A, NOVEMBER 2025 — THE BASICS — Safety Warnings, p.6

no.q: NEVER disassemble the suppressor beyond what is highlighted in this manual.
no.src: EOTECH DCBL SOUND SUPPRESSOR manual — SP2501 REV A, NOVEMBER 2025 — THE BASICS — Safety Warnings, p.6

steps.title: Titanium-safe cleaners only
steps.action: Read the label on your cleaner before any of it touches the can: the DCBL is titanium, and the cleaner has to be safe on titanium. Keep the gloves on for all of this.
steps.prose: Some suppressor cleaners are sold for steel. If the label does not say titanium is fine, pick another one.
steps.aside: EOTECH recommends cleaning at least every 2,000 rounds.
steps.quote: Because the DCBL suppressors are titanium, be sure to use cleaners that are safe on titanium.
steps.cite: EOTECH DCBL SOUND SUPPRESSOR manual — SP2501 REV A, NOVEMBER 2025 — MAINTENANCE — Cleaning, p.8
steps.warn: Before cleaning your suppressor, be sure to wear protective gloves to reduce any lead or contamination.

steps.title: Clean the body's threads
steps.action: Clean the threads on the suppressor body with a brush or a towel.
steps.prose: These are the threads the Hub came out of. Fouling left in them is what stops the Hub seating when you tighten it back down.
steps.quote: Clean threads on the suppressor body using a brush or towel.
steps.cite: EOTECH DCBL SOUND SUPPRESSOR manual — SP2501 REV A, NOVEMBER 2025 — MAINTENANCE — Cleaning, p.8

steps.title: Solvent for the main body
steps.action: Clean the main suppressor body with a solvent that breaks down lead and carbon fouling, used the way the solvent's own instructions say.
steps.prose: EOTech prints no soak time, so the time is the solvent maker's to give. What comes out carries lead: keep it off your skin.
steps.quote: To clean the main suppressor body, use a cleaning solvent that breaks down lead and carbon fouling. Follow the instructions of the solvent.
steps.cite: EOTECH DCBL SOUND SUPPRESSOR manual — SP2501 REV A, NOVEMBER 2025 — MAINTENANCE — Cleaning, p.8

steps.title: Blow it out until no liquid is left inside
steps.action: Once the body is clean, blow it out with a compressor and make sure the inside is free of liquids.
steps.prose: Wear eye protection and aim it away from you, because what comes out is solvent and lead. Nothing wet goes back on the rifle.
steps.quote: Once the body is clean, blow it out with a compressor and ensure the inside is free of liquids.
steps.cite: EOTECH DCBL SOUND SUPPRESSOR manual — SP2501 REV A, NOVEMBER 2025 — MAINTENANCE — Cleaning, p.8

steps.title: Put away somewhere safe and restricted
steps.action: When the can is off the rifle, store it in a safe, restricted area, with a muzzle device or thread protector on the barrel.
steps.prose: EOTech's legal warning is the reason for restricted: an unlocked suppressor at home with someone not registered to it may be treated as constructive possession.
steps.quote: Store your suppressor in a safe, restricted area.
steps.cite: EOTECH DCBL SOUND SUPPRESSOR manual — SP2501 REV A, NOVEMBER 2025 — GET STARTED — Removal, p.7

deepAbsentReason: EOTech's book prints one level of maintenance. Its MAINTENANCE page (printed p.8) takes the Hub off the suppressor body, cleans the threads and the body, and puts the Hub back, and all of that is in the routine lane above. The book prints no procedure past the Hub, and its Safety Warnings (printed p.6) state: 'NEVER disassemble the suppressor beyond what is highlighted in this manual.' This listing therefore has no deep clean.

cleaning.name: THREADS
tasks: Threads on the suppressor body cleaned with a brush or towel

cleaning.name: SUPPRESSOR BODY
tasks: Main body cleaned with a solvent that breaks down lead and carbon fouling
Solvent used by its own instructions
⛔ Never disassemble the suppressor past the Hub

cleaning.name: DRY INSIDE
tasks: Body blown out with a compressor

tasks: Muzzle device or thread protector back on the barrel
Suppressor stored in a safe, restricted area

reassembly: Suppressor body clean, and no liquid left inside.
Line the Hub threads up with the suppressor body's threads and slowly start turning clockwise. Do not cross-thread it.
Once you feel resistance, tighten the Hub firmly with the armorer's tool, to about 35 ft-lb.
Rifle unloaded, magazine out, safety on and the chamber looked at before the can goes back on.
If the KFM flash hider came off the barrel: it goes back on carefully, at about 30 ft-lb.

Onto a muzzle device: line the Hub threads up with the device's threads and engage them slowly. EOTech's installation page prints a clockwise rotation; its removal page says the KFM adapter uses reverse threads. Go with the direction the threads engage freely by hand. If neither does, stop and ask EOTech.
Direct thread: line the barrel threads up with the suppressor's and engage them slowly, clockwise.
Once you feel resistance, grip the suppressor firmly and tighten it hand tight, or to about 20 ft-lb.
fncheck: EOTech prints no function check for the can. With the rifle still unloaded: the Hub is tight in the body, the can is hand tight or at about 20 ft-lb, it went on without cross-threading, and the inside is free of liquid. Ammunition matches the caliber of the suppressor, and the barrel is at least 10.3 in. ⛔ EOTech warns that improper installation or use may result in serious injury or death: if it does not thread on cleanly, do not fire it, and contact EOTech.
